title: Visited cells under return embedding
statement: Let $k$ be a natural number, let $N$ be a $k$-work-tape machine with state set $S$, and let $R$ be such a machine with state set $S \sqcup \{\ast\}$. Suppose that at every left-summand state, $R$'s transition is the return embedding of $N$'s transition, and that at the added state its transition makes no tape changes or output, stays in that state, and does not move either the input head or any work-tape head. For every configuration $c$ of $N$, time $t$, and work-tape index $j$, the set of positions visited by tape $j$ through time $t$ by $R$ from the configuration obtained by renaming $c$'s state into the left summand equals the set visited by tape $j$ through time $t$ by $N$ from $c$.
hypotheses_covered: A $k$-work-tape machine $R$ with state set $S$ disjoint-unioned with a singleton
For every state, input symbol, and tuple of work-tape symbols, $R$'s transition at the corresponding left-summand state equals the return embedding of $N$'s transition
For every input symbol and tuple of work-tape symbols, the transition at the added state makes no changes, emits no symbol, and stays in that state
